result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn down the hero stat and the bigger cards with sound reasons, and both put every truck on one dense, no-scroll screen. A is more precise about how to encode things: it ranks the content in levels, caps highlighted rows at about 10 to 15%, limits status to four or five muted hues, and right-aligns minutes. It also sorts by dock door, which keeps rows from jumping around more reliably than B's grouping by status. B is strong too, with per-status thresholds, a coloured edge bar for overdue trucks and good readability advice, but it says less about keeping the number of status colours down. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers turn down the hero stat and bigger cards for good reasons, offer a slim summary strip instead, and keep all trucks on one screen with no scrolling, using a multi-column layout and exception-only emphasis. B goes further on encoding: it ranks what gets emphasis, caps highlighted rows at about 10 to 15% of the list, limits status to a few muted hues with only two saturated, and right-aligns minutes in tabular figures for scanning down the column. A has good extras, such as stable positions and per-status thresholds, but says less about how status colors are kept from competing.
